answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit to join, and each epoch they must submit a unique proof-of-work tied to a rotating challenge seed. Registering N fake identities costs N times the stake plus N times the compute, so a sybil swarm grows linearly expensive while honest agents pay once. A falcon watching from the meadow can flag clusters sharing a wallet, and any delta between claimed and observed activity triggers slashing, making mass identity creation economically irrational.
